page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz, with 8 physical cores and a single thread per core configuration. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between raw compute power and memory capacity. The instance exhibits poor single-core CPU performance and weak multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests. Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths are also weak. However, cached small-block memory read bandwidth is average at 400.15 GB/sec. The instance maintains average performance in database operations, Redis SET operations at 7.13 million operations per second, static web serving throughput, and Passmark CPU tests.

Given its high memory density and average database and Redis performance, the ecs.r6a.2xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive CPU processing. It is suited for in-memory caching, database operations, and web serving. It is less suitable for CPU-heavy tasks like physics simulations or multi-threaded decompression due to its weaker compute benchmark results.
